title: Two-instrument noise tests retain the known HD 1461 13.5-day velocity signal
abstract: We test a prior transfer result for the known HD 1461 velocity signal. We use 245 HARPS nights and 215 independent HIRES nights. We change the simulated errors in both instruments and fit the HARPS periods, phases and amplitudes again. All six 95 percent simulation ranges for HIRES error reduction remain above zero. The tests use 10-, 30- and 90-day noise blocks and two slow-trend models. A separate four-segment test checks a common wave. This is a model-based check of a known signal, not a new planet detection. Common stellar activity, fixed noise scales and local period limits remain important limits. Code, source hashes, aggregate results and retrieval instructions are included. External source rows are excluded.

display.caption: Error reduction ranges include simulated noise in both instruments. Segment amplitudes use fixed HARPS periods.

citations.reason: We reuse source selection, provenance and retrieval code, and test training uncertainty omitted from its transfer intervals.
